whatYouGet: A paper rich in real-life, competency-style questions that test understanding over rote work.

For a trustworthy answer key: paste the finished paper into a FRESH chat and ask it to solve and grade it as an unseen exam (it catches its own slips).
commonFix: If a question is just plain calculation, reply: 'Question [number] is not competency-based. Rewrite it around a real-life context that requires applying the concept, then re-verify the answer.'
promptText:
ROLE: Act as a mathematics paper-setter trained in competency-based and application-based assessment.

CONTEXT: This paper is for Class [CLASS/GRADE], [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / ICSE / State Board]. It must emphasise competency: real-life contexts, data interpretation, reasoning and multi-step application rather than rote calculation. Total marks [TOTAL MARKS], time [TIME].

YOUR TASK:
1. Make at least [PERCENT e.g. 60] percent of the marks competency-based (situational, applied, reasoning).
2. Include a balanced mix of MCQ, short and long competency items, with marks shown.
3. Keep contexts age-appropriate and relatable (money, travel, sports, health, shopping, etc.).
4. Provide a complete answer key that shows the reasoning, not only the final number.

INPUT: Chapters or topics to cover: [LIST CHAPTERS or TOPICS]. Use only these.

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Solve every question internally first, then verify each final answer twice by independent checks. Confirm the data given in each scenario is consistent and sufficient to solve. Never invent formulas or values. Keep mathematics legible in clean LaTeX or plain text. Ensure marks total exactly [TOTAL MARKS].

OUTPUT FORMAT, in this order:
1. HEADER BLOCK: 'Competency-Based Paper - Mathematics', class, board, time, maximum marks, 'Compiled by [YOUR NAME]'.
2. GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS: numbered.
3. THE PAPER: questions grouped by type, marks beside each, scenarios clearly set off from the sub-questions.
4. ANSWER KEY: final answer and the key reasoning step for every question.

RULES: Stay inside the listed syllabus. Scenarios must be solvable with the data given. Number every question. Marks total exactly.

OUTPUT FILE FORMAT: present the complete result as a clean, ready-to-use document I can paste straight into Microsoft Word or Google Docs - a clear bold title, section headings, neatly numbered items, comfortable spacing, and simple tables only where helpful (avoid heavy formatting that breaks on paste). It must also print cleanly to PDF on A4 (File > Print > Save as PDF). Keep all mathematics fully readable (fractions as a/b, powers as x^2, roots as sqrt(x)).

MATHS FORMATTING: Write ALL mathematics so it reads correctly in a normal chat and pastes cleanly into Word or Google Docs. Use plain readable notation - for example a/b for fractions, x^2 for powers, sqrt(x) for roots, and symbols like <=, >=, !=, +-, pi, theta, integral and sum. Do NOT output raw LaTeX or code such as \frac{}{}, \sqrt{}, x^{2}, $...$ or \( ... \) - these appear as broken symbols to a teacher in a free chat.

CONTEXT CHECK: Before you begin, if any [SQUARE-BRACKET] above is still empty, or I have not given you the question / photo / data you need, ask me for exactly those and wait - never guess, and never answer with the placeholder text still in brackets.

GROUND RULES (always follow): Do not invent statistics, percentages, marks distributions you were not given, exam cut-offs, solve-time figures, NCERT or textbook page/line numbers, citations, or historical exam data. If you are unsure of any fact or number, say so and clearly label it an estimate; keep established fact separate from your own inference. Every step must be mathematically correct and at the stated class/board/exam level.

title: Assertion-Reason Question Paper
whatYouGet: A paper of assertion-reason items with the standard four-option format and a clear key.
howToUse: Name your chapters and how many items, paste, and get correctly built assertion-reason questions.
effectiveUsage: 1. Paste the prompt into a chat.
2. Set the number of items.
3. List the chapters to cover.
4. Send and read each A and R pair.
5. Confirm the key matches the standard options.
For a trustworthy answer key: paste the finished paper into a FRESH chat and ask it to solve and grade it as an unseen exam (it catches its own slips).
commonFix: If an item's reason is unrelated, reply: 'In question [number] the Reason does not properly relate to the Assertion. Rewrite it so the option logic is clean, then update the key.'
promptText:
ROLE: Act as a mathematics paper-setter who specialises in assertion-reason questions.

CONTEXT: I need an ASSERTION-REASON paper for Class [CLASS/GRADE], [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / ICSE / State Board]. Number of items [NUMBER e.g. 15]. Each item uses the standard four options: (A) Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion; (B) Both are true but Reason is NOT the correct explanation; (C) Assertion true, Reason false; (D) Assertion false, Reason true.

YOUR TASK:
1. Write [NUMBER] items, each with a clear Assertion (A) and a Reason (R) drawn from the chapters below.
2. Spread the correct answers across all four option types, not just one.
3. Make the logic clean so exactly one option fits each item.
4. Provide an answer key with a one-line justification per item.

INPUT: Chapters or topics to cover: [LIST CHAPTERS or TOPICS]. Use only these.

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Decide internally whether each Assertion and each Reason is true, and whether the Reason explains the Assertion, then choose the option. Verify each item twice. Never invent formulas or values. Keep mathematics legible in clean LaTeX or plain text. Ensure exactly one option is correct per item.

OUTPUT FORMAT, in this order:
1. HEADER: 'Assertion-Reason Paper - Mathematics', class, board, total items, 'Compiled by [YOUR NAME]'.
2. THE OPTION KEY: the four standard options (A) to (D), stated once at the top.
3. THE ITEMS: numbered, each showing 'Assertion (A):' and 'Reason (R):'.
4. ANSWER KEY: item number, correct option letter, and a one-line reason.

RULES: Exactly one correct option per item. Spread answers across (A) to (D). Stay inside the listed syllabus. Number every item.

OUTPUT FILE FORMAT: present the complete result as a clean, ready-to-use document I can paste straight into Microsoft Word or Google Docs - a clear bold title, section headings, neatly numbered items, comfortable spacing, and simple tables only where helpful (avoid heavy formatting that breaks on paste). It must also print cleanly to PDF on A4 (File > Print > Save as PDF). Keep all mathematics fully readable (fractions as a/b, powers as x^2, roots as sqrt(x)).

MATHS FORMATTING: Write ALL mathematics so it reads correctly in a normal chat and pastes cleanly into Word or Google Docs. Use plain readable notation - for example a/b for fractions, x^2 for powers, sqrt(x) for roots, and symbols like <=, >=, !=, +-, pi, theta, integral and sum. Do NOT output raw LaTeX or code such as \frac{}{}, \sqrt{}, x^{2}, $...$ or \( ... \) - these appear as broken symbols to a teacher in a free chat.

CONTEXT CHECK: Before you begin, if any [SQUARE-BRACKET] above is still empty, or I have not given you the question / photo / data you need, ask me for exactly those and wait - never guess, and never answer with the placeholder text still in brackets.

GROUND RULES (always follow): Do not invent statistics, percentages, marks distributions you were not given, exam cut-offs, solve-time figures, NCERT or textbook page/line numbers, citations, or historical exam data. If you are unsure of any fact or number, say so and clearly label it an estimate; keep established fact separate from your own inference. Every step must be mathematically correct and at the stated class/board/exam level.

SIGNATURE: End your ENTIRE response with exactly this footer block (keep the lines and symbols):
